Bethany — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a concise checklist (attached) and included a short egress shaping snippet for your ops team. High-level guidance below so your engineers have quick answers: 

- Safety buffer: target 20% reserved capacity for burst absorption when you expect frequent 2x short bursts. If you can tolerate slightly higher tail latency for <5% of requests, 10–15% can be acceptable.
- Pod affinity: prefer dedicated-tenancy for BlueBridge’s critical inference routes (latency-sensitive). For batch/async workloads, mixed-tenant pools are fine and more cost-efficient.
- Admission control: soft admissions that allow short bursts but throttle sustained >1.5x baseline for >60s.
- Egress shaping: cap burst egress per node and add a small token-bucket at the VPC edge to protect upstream firewalls.

I attached two files: a one-page checklist and a minimal YAML egress snippet. If you want, we can run a 60-minute workshop with your ops team to walk through the checklist and test the YAML in staging.

Next step: can we schedule that workshop for Wed/Thu?

Bethany / Rachel — quick technical notes from infra perspective: 

- Sizing math: we mapped BlueBridge’s traces to our per-GPU sustained tokens/sec metric. With your sustained 1200 tps and expected 2x instantaneous bursts, plan for 3 GPUs per shard for critical endpoints (1.5 GPUs steady-state headroom + buffer). Use N+1 across racks to protect against single-rack failure.

- Safety buffer alternative: instead of a flat percent reserve, consider a token-based warm pool (2 nodes) that handle cold-cache priming/warmup spikes; this is more efficient for intermittent bursts and avoids idle reservation.

- Network/topology:
  - Prefer cross-rack NIC oversubscription limits set to 0.8 (to allow headroom).
  - Egress shaping: apply per-pod egress policers (100–200 Mbps depending on model size) and central token-bucket at the VPC egress to smooth aggregate spikes.

- Pod Affinity rule suggestion: critical routes -> node.selector: {role: priv-critical}, anti-affinity: "kube-topology.kubernetes.io/zone" to spread across hosts. Batch routes -> label: priv-batch, tolerate mixed best-effort.

Attaching a small YAML snippet for the egress policer we use in staging (also attached to this thread). Happy to join the ops workshop.

—Karthik

Quick answers for the workshop prep: 

- Warm-pool autoscale signal: prioritize GPU utilization (p99 across last 30s) together with request QPS slope. We use a composite rule: scale-up if p99 GPU util > 75% OR QPS slope > 40% over 30s; scale-down if p50 GPU util < 35% and QPS slope flat for 120s.
- Per-pod egress at 150Mbps: no, it shouldn’t change the 3-GPU shard guidance unless your model emits extremely large outputs frequently (>1MB per request). The egress cap mainly smooths network tail behavior; compute headroom and network headroom are orthogonal for ordinary models.

I’ve uploaded the checklist (privgpu-safety-buffer-checklist-v1.pdf) and the YAML snippets (network-egress-shaping-snippets.yaml) to the Drive link in the thread. Looking forward to the workshop.

—Grace
